title: Why Is the Sky Blue and Not Purple?
summary: Explains why the sky is blue: when sunlight strikes the molecules in the air, shorter wavelengths scatter more strongly (Rayleigh scattering). The episode traces the story from Tyndall's experiments to Rayleigh's eighteen seventy-one law of the inverse fourth power of wavelength, and on to Smoluchowski and Einstein showing that the scattering actually comes from tiny fluctuations in the density of the air. It also explains why the sky does not look purple even though violet light scatters even more: sunlight contains little violet, the atmosphere absorbs some of it, and our eyes are not very sensitive to violet. Finally, it looks at how ozone adds to the blue of twilight and why sunsets on Mars are blue.
